about: Falsifiable predictions for lab notes (fit-in-VRAM), written BEFORE any GPU run of these candidates on odie. Question: does a model whose weights and KV sit wholly in the two B70s' VRAM (vLLM XPU, no expert streaming) beat the served Flash-Next strata build (R8: 83.4 tok/s at 16 real agents, 32.6 at 1) on the real-trace replay? Do not edit the predicted numbers after the measurements land; add a 'measured' block beside them.
written_utc: 2026-10-27T16:05Z (before the GPU window; no booking yet)
recipe: odie 2x Arc Pro B70 (32 GB each), vLLM XPU llm-scaler 0.26.0-b2 flattened rootfs (our patched copy, b70-vllm.sh launcher: eager, fp8 KV, prefix caching, chunked prefill 8192, block 64, MTP off unless stated), data-parallel: one TP1 instance per card behind one port (dp-affinity-proxy: a conversation sticks to one card, new conversations split evenly), MAX_MODEL_LEN 262144, 8 seqs per card. Replay: agent-replay.py run --trace agent-long-16 --warmup-s 600 --duration-s 600, 16 agents x2 runs and 1 agent x1.
equation: useful = 1 / (1 / D + F / P) (src/model.js agentThroughput, stall=true: vLLM's chunked prefill shares every engine step, so a read displaces decode like a strata read stalls it). 1 agent adds the tool-gap term: useful_1 = o / (o / D1 + F x o / P1 + g), o = 272 output tokens a turn and g = 1.70 s of replayed tool gap a turn (MEASURED on R8's n1 run: 19,574 tokens and 122.3 s over 72 turns, same trace, gap_scale 1). At 16 agents the gaps are filled by other agents' work (gap share ~8 % of an agent's cycle), so no gap term there (INFERRED). Resident prefill per read of T fresh tokens at context depth d: t(T) = t_pass + (T + r) x (m + a x d).

anchors_for_qfn: B70 prefill with every weight resident, 3B-active hybrid MoE: 3.4-3.9k tok/s on real agent growth reads at 15-120k depth, 3.7-4.3k cold (32k-64k). R8 Flash-Next reads 0.85-1.08k: the expert stream costs ~3.5-4x at agent read sizes (INFERRED, different model and engine).
Eager vLLM decode on a B70 is launch-overhead-bound: ~37-40 tok/s per stream from short to 64k depth, and 8 streams cost almost nothing extra at short depth (319 total); at 32k, 8 streams ~190 total.

Hybrid (GatedDeltaNet) prefix cache in vLLM 'align' mode hits only on 2,048-token boundaries here (cached tokens 14336, 18432, 20480, ... = multiples of 2048): every turn re-reads up to 2,047 tokens, F_reread 7.7 at one agent vs R8's 2.6. Cause INFERRED (state saved at chunk boundaries; block 64, long-prefill 2048).
turns_per_agent_min at 1 agent: Ornith 7.7 vs R8 7.2: a 4x faster prefill bought only +7 % turns because decode (58 vs 69 tok/s) and the larger re-read F offset it
measured.prediction_check_not_scored: For the record only: the n1 1-agent useful 39.8 sits inside the predicted 38-62 band (51.4 point); P_1 3.45k vs 2.09k predicted (+65 %, model too pessimistic on resident prefill at depth); D_1 58 vs 90 predicted (-35 %, eager overhead). 16-agent: not measured.

rescore_turn_model.about: Re-score with the per-turn agent model (src/model.js agentReplaySim; data/workload.json turn_model), added after the measurements; the predictions above stay as written. before = this file's own numbers (turns derived where the old model gave only useful tok/s: its useful / the run's measured output a turn); after = the model with every input; held_out = the same with the inputs measured on the scored run replaced by what existed without it (each input's held_out value, else the fallbacks turn_model states). after_at_commit = the model's numbers when this block was written (tests/test_workload.js checks they still hold). node report.js --accuracy prints the table
